beyond.copy:
BEYOND THE FRAME | Experimental Short Film

Beyond the Frame is a solo experimental film exploring the sublime — the moment when fear, beauty and awe begin to exist together.

I wanted to examine whether fear must always end in discomfort, or whether it can become a path towards curiosity and liberation. The film begins in a quiet, limited environment before gradually expanding into light, abstraction and an infinite white space.

The starburst sequence was influenced by the wormhole scene in 2001: A Space Odyssey. It became a visual transition between the physical world and something larger than the visible frame.

I completed the cinematography, editing, colour grading, visual effects and sound-design layering independently.

Created in 2025.

Credits:
Film, editing, VFX and sound design by Thuy An Ngo.

lullaby.copy:
ENDLESS LULLABY | Experimental Multisensory Animation

Endless Lullaby is an experimental animation exploring the uncanny, childhood trauma and a fictional cycle of repeated harm.

The project uses dolls because they exist between familiarity and discomfort. Their faces and bodies resemble people, but their stillness can make them feel strangely lifeless. Through repetition, unusual compositions, restrained movement and distorted sound, familiar childhood objects gradually become unsettling.

The story refers sensitively to a child whose personal and bodily boundaries are violated, and to the way unresolved trauma may continue across time. The experience is communicated through metaphor rather than explicit imagery.

I developed the main visual compositions, illustrated the dolls and toy assets, contributed to the storyboard, and worked across animation and compositing.

fresh.copy:
FRESH UP | AI-Assisted Experimental Commercial

Fresh Up is an experimental commercial exploring visceral design and cross-modal perception — how an image or sound can create an imagined physical response in the body.

To me, “visceral” describes something felt in the gut before it is fully understood by the mind. I used food because our senses interact with it every day. Toothpaste and cream can appear similar in colour and texture, but their tastes and purposes are completely different. Placing mint toothpaste on greasy pizza interrupts this expectation and creates discomfort without using violence or gore.

The visual direction draws on 1990s infomercials, using bright product imagery, excessive close-ups, VHS noise and unusual colour. Wet, sticky and slurping sounds strengthen the imagined taste and texture.

AI was used to generate source footage. I directed the concept and completed the prompt development, footage selection, editing, colour treatment, compositing and VHS-effect layering.

Created in 2025.

#ExperimentalCommercial #VisceralDesign #CrossModalPerception #AIFilm #MotionDesign

eyes.copy:
WHEN EYES DON’T BLINK | Experimental Animation

When Eyes Don’t Blink is an experimental animation developed through an investigation into the uncanny and multisensory storytelling. The work explores how restrained movement, repetition, stillness and sound can make a familiar image feel subtly wrong.

Rather than relying on direct horror imagery, the animation builds discomfort through timing and sensory tension. Small changes in movement and audio encourage the viewer to notice what is absent, delayed or unnaturally still.

Created in collaboration with Sound Design students.
